messages:
sara_support: FYI customer ACME reporting 429s but Console shows ~90% of quota remaining. Escalating. ticket: #2345.

jane_acme: repro notes from our app — at 2026-03-16T18:12:03Z we saw a 200, then 3x 429s in the next 10s. Console token panel for our tenant (acme-prod) shows 9,200 tokens available for the current window. Request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, tenant: acme-prod.

aj_eng: thanks — can you paste the full request headers (x-request-id, x-tenant, x-route) and the exact timestamps? also which Console view are you looking at (per-tenant topology or org-wide)?

sara_support: pasted below. route: POST /v1/generate (generation.create). headers: 
```
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
x-tenant-id: acme-prod
x-route: generation.create
```
timestamps: 2026-03-16T18:12:03Z..18:12:13Z. Console view: tenant -> quota -> current-window.

ingest-bot: detected kafka partition lag spike: topic=quota-events partition=12 lag from 2026-03-16T18:09:20Z to 2026-03-16T18:11:40Z, ingest throughput dropped ~85%. See alert: https://mon.redwood.internal/alerts/qa-1782

mike_prod: quick hypothesis: we recently added "sparse rollup" compaction for very-low-throughput tenants to reduce cardinality. It compacts tiny increments into a spillover bucket and emits a single delta per minute. looks like an edge-case where a compacted delta landed in prev-window boundary; Console shows the materialized rollup (post-compaction) but the enforcer reads near-real-time increments. If the increment was compacted and the enforcer voted on a slightly later window the counts can diverge. Not the usual off-by-one but a sparse-rollup spillover race.

aj_eng: can we get a reproducible script? sara, can ACME try a quick local repro: 5 requests of 10 tokens each, spaced 300ms apart. If first request goes through and the next ones 429, that matches. Also requesting the enforcer logs around the x-request-id to see which window key it checked (e.g., tenant:acme-prod:window:2026-03-16T18:12:00).

sara_support: ACME ran the test and attached the logs: first request 200, then 429s for the rest. Enforcer log snippet shows: 
```
[2026-03-16T18:12:04Z] enforcer.check tenant=acme-prod window=2026-03-16T18:12:00 key=tenant:acme-prod:win:2026-03-16T18:12:00 tokens_used=48 limit=100
[2026-03-16T18:12:05Z] enforcer.check tenant=acme-prod window=2026-03-16T18:12:00 key=tenant:acme-prod:win:2026-03-16T18:12:00 tokens_used=148 limit=100 -> 429
```
Console panel snapshot at 18:12:10 shows tokens_used=48 for that same window (UI materialized value).

mike_prod: that log is golden. It means the enforcer saw the compaction/delta replay differently than the UI materializer did. Two paths: 1) the materializer reads compacted rollups (coalesced) and applied them in a later commit so UI lags, or 2) the enforcer used raw increments and double-counted a spillover when a replay came in. I'm leaning to (1) but need to check the rollup consumer offsets.

aj_eng: run this ClickHouse-ish query against quota_rollups to compare raw increments vs rollup counts in the same window (replace tenant):
```
SELECT tenant, window_start,
  sum(raw_tokens) AS raw_sum,
  sum(compacted_tokens) AS rollup_sum
FROM quota_events
WHERE tenant='acme-prod' AND window_start >= toDateTime('2026-03-16 18:11:00')
GROUP BY tenant, window_start
ORDER BY window_start DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

ingest-bot: consumer offsets for topic=quota-rollups partition=12 show a 68s rebalance around 18:10:50 — some messages were reprocessed and a compacted delta was emitted at 18:11:40.

mike_prod: confirmed — there was a short consumer rebalancing that caused the compacted spillover to be emitted late. UI materializer pulled the compacted delta and wrote it into the materialized view at 18:12:10, but enforcer was enforcing against raw increments at 18:12:05 (race). Net effect: enforcement saw the increment earlier than the materialized UI did, so the UI temporarily looked like there were tokens available.

aj_eng: mitigation plan: patch enforcer to check an adjacent previous window key if the current window looks under-counted (safe fallback for 60s). I'll open PR and push a canary to us-east-1 only. Also will add high-cardinality telemetry to detect similar races.

mike_prod: long-term: change compaction to emit a tombstone+delta atomically or push materializer to subscribe to the same consumer group so it won't lag behind.

sara_support: interim customer response: apologized + explained technical cause, offered 5% billing credit for the impacted minute and instructions to rate-limit retries for 1 minute. ACME accepted.

jane_acme: thanks for quick turn. we'll follow the replay test and confirm once canary is up.

aj_eng: PR 4321 opened: https://git.redwood/internal/pr/4321 — canary deploy scheduled in 20m. will update here when live.

sara_support: noting done for ticketing and will close once ACME verifies. :white_check_mark:
